title: The Days a Covered Value Is Spread Across on a Protection Claim
content:
Where the value a Pass and Trip Protection plan covers is taken in proportion to time, the days it is spread
across are settled as follows.

1. Where cover began on or before the day the season opened and the plan's waiting period ended after cover
   began, the value is spread across the days from the first day of the season the plan covers to its last
   day.
2. Where cover began after the day the season opened, the value is spread across the days from the day cover
   began to the day cover is due to end.
3. In every other case the value is spread across the days from the day the plan's waiting period ended to the
   day cover is due to end.

**The conditions put side by side.**

| Cover began | The waiting period ended after cover began | The value is spread across |
| --- | --- | --- |
| On or before the day the season opened | Yes | The days from the season's first day to its last day |
| On or before the day the season opened | No | The days from the day the waiting period ended to the day cover is due to end |
| After the day the season opened | Either | The days from the day cover began to the day cover is due to end |

**Points of judgement (hypothetical inputs).** A plan whose cover began on the very day the season opened, and
whose waiting period of 10 days ended after that, is spread across the whole season. A plan whose cover began
on the day the season opened and which carries no waiting period at all, so that the waiting period does not
end after cover began, falls to the third case and is spread across the days from the end of the waiting
period to the day cover is due to end. A plan whose cover began a fortnight into the season is spread across
the days from the day cover began to the day cover is due to end, whatever its waiting period.
